parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **production**?

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **productivity**?
choices: Splitting the production process into separate tasks with each worker specialising in one task
Output per unit of input such as output per worker per hour
The output produced per worker or per hour worked over a period of time
Production that uses a high proportion of machinery/capital relative to labour

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (Output per unit of input such as output per worker per hour)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of division of labour
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour productivity
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of capital-intensive production

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **profit maximisation**?
choices: When two firms at the same stage of production in the same industry join together
When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest
When a firm grows by joining with another firm through a merger or takeover
When two firms at different stages of production in the same industry join together

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of horizontal integration
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of external growth
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of vertical integration

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **organic growth**?

When two firms agree to join together to form one firm

rows.answer:

B: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit maximisation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of external growth
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of merger

rows.answer:

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of market share

parts.text: Describe one reason why a firm may decide to grow.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for a relevant point and 1 mark for a linked development, for example:
- to benefit from economies of scale (1), which reduce average costs (1)
- to spread risk (1) by selling in more markets so a fall in one is offset (1)
- to increase market power (1), allowing more control over prices (1)
rows.notes: Only one point should be credited. A second, undeveloped point does not gain the development mark.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **economies of scale**?
choices: The increase in average costs that occurs when a firm grows beyond a certain size
The reduction in average costs that occurs as a firm increases its scale of production
Lower average costs from buying inputs in bulk so suppliers give discounts
Lower average costs from using larger or more advanced machinery that only big firms can afford

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The reduction in average costs that occurs as a firm increases its scale of production)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of diseconomies of scale
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of purchasing economies of scale
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of technical economies of scale

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **diseconomies of scale**?
choices: The reduction in average costs that occurs as a firm increases its scale of production

Lower average costs because large firms can borrow more cheaply and easily than small firms

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The increase in average costs that occurs when a firm grows beyond a certain size)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of economies of scale
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of external economies of scale
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of financial economies of scale

Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Purchasing economies of scale (1): Zephyr Partners buys goods in very large quantities for 219 shops (1), so suppliers give bulk discounts, lowering its average costs (1)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **monopoly**?
choices: A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions)
A firm that can set the price of its product because it has market power
Competing using factors other than price such as branding, quality or advertising
A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions))
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of price maker
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-price competition
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of oligopoly

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **oligopoly**?
choices: Competing using factors other than price such as branding, quality or advertising
A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent
A firm that must accept the market price because it is too small to influence it
When firms agree to work together for example to fix prices, rather than compete

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-price competition
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of price taker
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of collusion

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **competitive market**?

A market with many firms none of which can control the market price
A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions)
A firm that must accept the market price because it is too small to influence it

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A market with many firms none of which can control the market price)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-price competition
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of monopoly
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of price taker

When firms agree to work together for example to fix prices, rather than compete

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **privatisation**?
choices: The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector
The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the private sector to the public sector/state
Government action to prevent abuse of market power and promote competition between firms
The removal of rules and restrictions on firms in order to increase competition

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of nationalisation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of competition policy
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **nationalisation**?
choices: The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the private sector to the public sector/state
The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector
The removal of rules and restrictions on firms in order to increase competition
A market where one firm can supply at a lower average cost than two or more firms could, such as water pipes

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the private sector to the public sector/state)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of privatisation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of natural monopoly

Rules set by government or a regulator to control how firms behave

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of nationalisation
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of natural monopoly

grid.descriptor: No rewardable material.
